name: D. Carver & Co.

proprietors.name: David Carver
proprietors.basis: The register matches the printed name to the town card carver_david (action: enrich), so this is the same person the resident layer already holds. Dated by the printing window, which bounds the reading and does not date the partnership.

staff.name: Joseph Hubbard
staff.basis: The staffing model puts 2 of this role in a lumber yard at the typical band and 3 at the high end, on period_convention. A yard is piled and loaded by hand. Analogue: the forwarding houses above, whose warehouse labour this model prices the same way. This person is a reconstructed resident of the trade with no workplace of their own; the house is one the business layer already holds, and this row points at it rather than raising anything. Seated by tools/seat_reconstructed_trades_1835.py (T-1433) off 1835_business_staffing_model#lumber_yard.labourer; carried onto this record by tools/staff_the_houses_1835.py (T-1462).
staff.replaceable_by: a source naming where this person worked, which retires the draw

staffing.basis: the 1835 business staffing model's band for this class, with the reconstructed seats T-1433 put in this house marked drawn

shortfall.statement: The staffing model puts 2 hand(s) about this kind of house at its typical band and this house carries 1. It stands 1 short, and stands short rather than being quietly filled.
shortfall.counted_here: the reconstructed hands this overlay seats. A hand a SOURCE names carries its own citation in staff[] and is counted by the attested join, not by this.

locations.basis: The register resolved no place for this house at the scene date.

dates.basis: No opening is announced. The first printing, 1834-09-10, is the bound: the house was trading by then and the record does not say when it began.
